correctness.rationale: The RKHS residual equals the origin-to-convex-hull distance. Uniform cyclic spacings are Dirichlet; one gap exceeds half a circle at most, giving exact conditional beta survival. Central symmetry and strict convexity provide a supporting missing-gap chord; uniform small-gap projection to that chord and a Taylor determinant expansion give the conditional exponential mixture. A feasible midpoint uniformly bounds E_N by a Lipschitz constant times gap deficit, proving uniform integrability of scaled squared errors. The ellipse integral gives J(g)=ab. The finite verification program (standard library) passed 5746 checks; the proof, not these checks, justifies all N and the limit.

originality.rationale: The classical exact non-inclusion probability and isotropic spacing tail are attributed to prior results, not counted as novel. The assessed claim is the conditional error-size distribution for a general smooth centrally symmetric feature curve, its uniformly justified transfer to the mean-square limit, and the sharp shape integral J(g), equal to ab for anisotropic first-harmonic kernels. Relevant source mathematics is compared by implication, not title; none of the material inspected supplies that conditional geometric coefficient. Residual unindexed random-polytope literature is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Conditional rare center-distance limits may exist under alternate names in the extensive geometric probability and random-polytope literature; not all works were accessible in full text.
The isotropic circle tail and exact zero-error probability follow from classical circular spacings and Wendel, so they are explicitly excluded from the originality-bearing part.
An unstated stronger theorem in a relevant unindexed original might subsume the smooth-curve shape law.

value.rationale: This is an exact natural risk invariant for a recently studied fixed-pool positive-weight KQ setting, not an arbitrary parameter slice: it quantifies both the probability and severity of unavoidable positive-weight error and gives a sharp anisotropic constant ab instead of loose semiaxis bounds. The conditional exponential-mixture law explains the difference between rare failure and its magnitude, and the circle tail supplies an exactly checkable benchmark. Relevance is confined to finite-rank angular kernels; no generic improvement over established infinite-rank bounds is claimed.
